answer: Think of the network as a meadow where honest agents graze on shared rewards. A sybil attacker scatters a thousand fake seeds, each sprouting a juniper that looks alive from afar. The defense: each epoch the randomness beacon summons random identities to do a short, time-boxed verification task — as if demanding every plant on the knoll prove it photosynthesizes now. One honest agent answers one summons easily. The farmer must do real graded work for a thousand summons, so cost scales with identities while rewards do not. Fakes wither: attention, unlike identity, cannot be counterfeited.
